summary: pylever 1.0.10 exfiltrates Discord tokens and browser secrets to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: The package scans Chrome, Edge, and Brave browser storage (LevelDB and Cache directories under the user's AppData) and the Discord desktop client's Roaming data for strings matching the Discord auth token regex. On Windows it invokes PowerShell to call System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData.Unprotect via subprocess, DPAPI-decrypting the current user's encrypted browser storage to recover cleartext token material. Recovered tokens are validated against discord.com/api, and valid tokens are POSTed along with the associated account username, user id, email, verification status, and bot flag to a hardcoded Discord webhook URL (discord.com/api/webhooks/1547416857537945601/...). The webhook destination is baked into module-level state and cannot be overridden by callers, so any use of the public _Client API routes captured credentials to the author's endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
